newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares jumped to a new record close on Wednesday with stocks pushed higher by a firm dollar and a rising Wall Street.
The AEX share index touched a new all-time high at 967.02 points and ended at a new record close of 965.25, 16.09 points, or 1.7 percent, higher than Tuesday's close.
The AMX Midcap index showed an even stronger rise, gaining 2.32 percent or 34.13 points to 1508.30.
Software firm Baan and semiconductor maker ASM Lithography were the main two winners in the AMX.
Dealers said some participants were nervous ahead of Friday's options expiry.
"Many options will be extended," said one dealer, with another noting that only a sudden change in market sentiment could disrupt the market in combination with the expiry.
He said this could happen if there was currency intervention involving the dollar, but added there was no great likelihood in the short-run.
The dollar was steady at its recent high level, trading at 2.0256 guilders versus 1.9874 a week ago.
Electronics firm Philips jumped to a new high.
Philips rose 6.80 guilders to 157.80 and touched a high of 158.50 ahead of its second quarter results, which will be published on July 24.
Insurer Aegon gave another strong performance, rising 2.30 guilders to 158.50. The stock has risen over 10 guilders in the last week.
Semiconductor maker ASM International zoomed up, rising almost 20 percent or 4.90 guilders to 29.70 amid general positive sentiment for high-techs.
